Subject: Follow-up: encryption & key management discovery

Thanks for the demo earlier — quick follow-up notes from our side and a couple of clarifying questions. Appreciate the concise walkthrough of Redwood Dedicated vs Private for our PHI workload.

Short summary of our priorities: 
- We must support HIPAA controlled PHI in-region (US) and have a customer-managed key option for at-rest encryption.
- We need to understand where HSMs fit in (BYOK vs Redwood-managed CMKs) and what the operational implications are for key rotation and emergency key revocation.
- SOC 2 Type II report and evidence for encryption/configuration controls will be required for our procurement team.

A few clarifying questions: 
1) Can Redwood Private be deployed in our VPC and integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM (we prefer to keep key material in our account)?
2) If Redwood manages keys, what are the retention and key escrow policies?
3) Do you support in-transit TLS mutual auth with client certs, and is that configurable per-route?

Attached: PulseCare_Security_Assessment_v1.pdf (our high-level security intake).

Thanks — Alicia

Alicia — great to speak earlier. Short post-call recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap (brief):
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (not suitable for PHI), Dedicated, Private. Private supports customer VPC with a private control plane.
- Key options: Redwood-managed keys (default, easier), Customer-managed keys in customer's KMS (BYOK) via cross-account integration, and HSM-backed CMKs for FIPS-level requirements.
- Networking: mTLS + private peering supported for Private deployments.

Questions answered: 
1) VPC + AWS KMS: Yes, Private can run in your VPC and integrate with your AWS KMS. We support a cross-account role and envelope encryption so the root key material stays in your AWS account.
2) Redwood-managed keys: We provide key lifecycle logs and rotation policies; Redwood does not escrow customer symmetric key material by default — but we can discuss escrow for enterprise contracts.
3) mTLS: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and can configure mutual TLS for customer endpoints; per-route auth is supported through our gateway config.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Laura (cc) will initiate the vendor security questionnaire and request SOC 2 Type II artifacts.
- PulseCare to confirm desired key custody model (BYOK via AWS KMS vs Redwood HSM CMK).
- PRIO: We’ll prepare a technical note outlining the KMS integration steps and typical timeline for a Private deployment POC (estimate 3–4 weeks).

Attachments: Redwood_KMS_options.docx (high-level options matrix).

I'll schedule a follow-up 30-min technical call next week to walk engineering through the integration. If PulseCare prefers, we can include our cryptography engineer.

Thanks,

Alicia / Tom — thanks for the quick responses. A couple operational notes and an actionable mutual action plan (MAP) to keep momentum: 

MAP (owners & timeline):
- PulseCare: complete the vendor questionnaire and provide SOC 2 Type II (owner: Alicia; due: 2027-06-09)
- Redwood: deliver KMS integration playbook + sample CloudFormation role (owner: Karthik; due: 2027-06-11)
- Joint: schedule 60-min engineering walkthru to validate cross-account IAM and network firewall rules (owner: PulseCare + Redwood; target week of 2027-06-14)

Notes on key custody: 
- For BYOK via AWS KMS: we use envelope encryption where Redwood holds only encrypted DEKs; customer CMK in their account unwraps. Key rotation is supported without re-encrypting object blobs.
- For HSM-backed Redwood CMKs: we can provide an HSM-backed CMK option (FIPS capable) but this requires an elevated contract and carve-out for key export/escrow — we documented options in the attached Redwood_KMS_options.docx.
